title: A round from an intermediate-state cut
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine, let $a,e$ be states, and let $c$ be a configuration. Suppose $c$ is in state $a$, $t>0$, and at each time $u$ with $0<u<t$ the machine is in a state $s$ different from both $a$ and $e$. If at time $t$ the machine is in state $a$ or $e$, then the run from $c$ to its configuration at time $t$ is a round from $a$ with escape set consisting of the optional state $e$ and with the head-position property that holds everywhere.
hypotheses_covered: At every intermediate time $0<u<t$, the state is some $s$ distinct from $a$ and $e$
At time $t$, the state is $a$ or $e$
